title: ISW Cross-Correlation Predictions for Energy-Flow Cosmology with DESI DR1 Tracers
description: This paper computes the CMB–galaxy ISW cross-correlation C_ell^{Tg} for Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) using linear perturbation theory and DESI DR1–motivated tracer windows over multipoles ell=2–60. It introduces a bounded cancellation index C that isolates opposite-sign contributions from the standard ISW kernel and an EFC transition kernel driven by a time-varying gravitational coupling mu(a). The key prediction is a strong, redshift-dependent suppression of the ISW amplitude near the EFC transition epoch (z_t ≈ 0.82), providing clear falsifiable tests against ΛCDM.

growth_equation.latex: D'' + \left(2 + \frac{d\ln H}{dx}\right) D' - \frac{3}{2} \/ \Omega_m(a)\, \mu(a)\, D = 0, \quad x \equiv \ln a
growth_equation.description: Linear growth of matter perturbations in EFC, where the effective Poisson coupling mu(a) modifies the source term.

modified_poisson.description: Modified Poisson equation encoding the time-dependent gravitational coupling mu(a) in EFC.

mu_parameterization.description: Transition parameterization for the effective coupling mu(a), centered at a_t with width sigma_cos and amplitude beta.

isw_kernel_decomposition.description: Decomposition of the ISW kernel into a standard term K_mu and an EFC transition term K_mu' arising from time variation of mu(a).

cancellation_metric.description: Bounded metric quantifying opposite-sign cancellation between the standard ISW and transition contributions; C→1 indicates near-total cancellation.

w_background_perturbation.description: Smooth, percent-level background perturbation used for sensitivity checks; results found stable with max \Delta\chi^2 < 1 on 14 RSD points.

key_results.main_finding: EFC predicts strong redshift-dependent cancellation (high C) between K_mu and K_mu' near z_t ≈ 0.82, suppressing the ISW amplitude (AISW ≈ 0.3–0.6) relative to ΛCDM, with current measurements consistent within ~1.6σ.
datasets_used: DESI DR1-motivated tracer windows (LRGz0, LRG+ELG, ELG)
Galaxy bias from DESI DR1 full-shape analyses (Adame et al. 2025)
Planck temperature maps (for benchmarking with published results)
DESI Legacy Survey × Planck ISW (Hang et al. 2021)
ATLAS LRG × Planck redshift-binned ISW (Ansarinejad et al. 2020)
RSD compilation (14 points) for sensitivity checks

sealed_predictions.statement: The cancellation index C increases monotonically with tracer overlap with the transition epoch z_t ≈ 0.82: C ≈ 0.59 (LRGz0, z_eff ≈ 0.51), C ≈ 0.79 (LRG+ELG, z_eff ≈ 0.93), and C ≈ 0.96 (ELG, z_eff ≈ 1.32).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic DESI × Planck (or equivalent CMB T) ISW cross-correlation across spectroscopic bins spanning z≈0.4–1.4, testing monotonic C(z_eff).

sealed_predictions.statement: ISW amplitude is suppressed for tracers overlapping z_t, with AISW ≈ 0.3–0.6 over ℓ=2–60, while ΛCDM predicts AISW = 1 for all tracers.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Amplitude fits to tomographic DESI spectroscopic bins overlapping z_t that yield AISW ≈ 1.0 ± 0.1 (or higher) with C ≈ 0.

sealed_predictions.statement: The ISW signal shape in ℓ is only mildly altered relative to ΛCDM; the distinctive signature is an amplitude suppression and large C near z_t rather than a strong ℓ-dependent distortion.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multipole-resolved C_ell^{Tg} measurements in ℓ=2–60 showing ΛCDM-like amplitudes across all bins overlapping z_t without suppression.

sealed_predictions.statement: Opposite-sign contributions from K_mu and K_mu' near z_t produce partial cancellation, with the signed fraction from K_mu' exceeding unity in magnitude when near-cancellation occurs (bounded by C, not by signed fraction).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Template-decomposition or parameter-inference analyses that robustly exclude opposite-sign kernel contributions near z_t when fitting EFC parameterization to tomographic C_ell^{Tg}.

kill_criteria: KC1: Tomographic DESI spectroscopic bins overlapping z_t ≈ 0.82 yield AISW = 1.0 ± 0.1 with C ≈ 0 over ℓ=2–60.
KC2: The measured cancellation index C does not increase with tracer effective redshift across bins bracketing z_t (monotonicity violated at >3σ).
KC3: A joint fit to tomographic C_ell^{Tg} near z_t prefers β ≈ 0 (i.e., μ(a) ≈ 1 with no transition) and rejects β = 0.16, a_t ≈ 0.55 for all σ_cos with Δχ^2 ≫ 10.
KC4: High-precision measurements show AISW ≥ 0.9 in bins centered near z_t with uncertainties ≤ 0.1, inconsistent with the predicted 0.3–0.6 suppression.
abstract: Computes ISW-galaxy cross-correlation C_ℓ^Tg for EFC using linear perturbation theory, introducing the cancellation metric C to quantify opposite-sign contributions from standard and transition kernels.

falsification_criteria.EFC_falsified_if: Tomographic bins overlapping z_t yield A_ISW = 1.0 ± 0.1 and C ≈ 0
falsification_criteria.LCDM_challenged_if: A_ISW ≪ 1 with high C at z_t
falsification_criteria.decisive_test: Tomographic C_ℓ^Tg in DESI spectroscopic bins overlapping z_t

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first sealed, quantitative ISW cross-correlation predictions for EFC using DESI DR1 tracer windows, introducing the cancellation index C as a novel EFC-specific diagnostic. It opens a new observable channel (tomographic C_ell^{Tg}) with four paper-level kill criteria and four sealed predictions anchored to the mu(a) transition at z_t ≈ 0.82. Current data are consistent with the predicted suppression (AISW ≈ 0.3–0.6) within ~1.6σ, but the decisive test awaits DESI spectroscopic tomographic bins overlapping z_t.
graph_insights: This paper is currently an isolated node in the graph (no 1-2 hop connections found), indicating a genuinely new observable channel for EFC. It should be linked to: (a) the f σ_8 sealed prediction paper via the shared μ(a) parameterisation and growth factor D(a), (b) any future EFCLASS Boltzmann solver work since the Eisenstein–Hu transfer function is an acknowledged approximation, and (c) DESI DR1/DR2 RSD papers via the same tracer windows and galaxy bias calibration.

The absence of validation tests sharing ISW observables confirms this opens a previously uncovered test axis — total active test count should increase from 101 to 107 (6 new tests added), survived from 91 to 94 (3 passing now), pipeline from 18 to 21 (3 planned/pending).

implicit_consequences: The cancellation index C provides a model-independent null test: any modified-gravity theory with μ(a)≠1 but different transition parameters will produce a different C(z) profile, making C a discriminator not just against ΛCDM but among competing MG models.

The ISW suppression prediction is degenerate-breaking for the f σ_8 sealed prediction at z=0.7: if DESI DR2 confirms f σ_8 ≈ 0.430 AND ISW shows AISW < 0.6 near z_t, both signals corroborate the same μ(a) transition, creating a joint two-observable consistency lock.

The paper implicitly requires the EFCLASS Boltzmann solver (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver gap) for a full beyond-Limber, beyond-Eisenstein-Hu treatment; the parametric transfer function used here is a placeholder that must be replaced before confrontation with Stage-IV precision data.

The z̄ ≈ 0.68 ISW null reported by Ansarinejad et al. 2020 is naturally accommodated by EFC's cancellation mechanism — this is not explicitly flagged as a retrodiction but effectively functions as one.

ACT and SO lensing × galaxy cross-correlations at similar redshifts will probe the same μ(a) transition through the lensing potential rather than its time derivative, providing an independent cross-check of the kernel decomposition.
